newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight rates soften with ample supply.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight rates soften with ample supply.

text.p: MANILA, Dec 12 - Philippine overnight money softened on Tuesday, ending three-straight days of rise as enough cash flooded the system after banks sold dollars, traders said.
"Most banks were able to improve their liquidity after selling down their dollars to a big company on Wednesday," said one dealer in a major Philippine bank.
The average reached 11.0625 percent from the previous 12.0.
Volume eased to 19.451 billion pesos from the previous 25.372 billion.
There were 33 lenders while there were 25 borrowers.
"Early borrowers were slapped a higher rate of 12.25 percent," said one dealer.
Rates later hit a low of 10.8125 percent as more lenders emerged in the market, he said.
Rates are expected to soften further on Friday with more cash in the system, they said.
Secondary trading in government securities was quiet.
A Reuters survey of seven banks showed three-month bills were being bidded at 11.50 to 11.70 percent and offered at 11.40 to 11.575 percent.

Six-month bills were bidded at 11.826 to 12 percent and offered at 11.725 to 11.825 percent, and one-year bills were bidded at 12.25 to 12.5 percent and offered at 12.1 to 12.225 percent. --DOLLY AGLAY (632) 841-89-36, FAX 817-62-67
